title: Broadcom Sinks 9% as AI Regulation Fears Deepen Chip Rout
excerpt: The chipmaker had no news of its own, but a post-midterm scare over data center limits and AI rules knocked more than 10 percent off the semiconductor index.
body:
• Broadcom shares fell about 9 percent on Thursday in a broad AI chip rout, with no company-specific news behind the drop.
  • Traders blamed fears that Democratic midterm wins will bring tighter AI rules and slower data center construction; the Philadelphia semiconductor index fell more than 10 percent.
  • Nvidia fell 8.6 percent, Micron 15 percent and Qualcomm about 10 percent; the Nasdaq dropped more than 4 percent into correction territory.
  • Broadcom's own outlook is unchanged for now: it guided in September to $21.7 billion of fiscal fourth-quarter AI chip revenue, and its next report lands December 9.

Broadcom shares sank about 9 percent on Thursday as investors sold the entire AI supply chain on fears that the new political landscape in Washington will slow the data center build-out the chip boom depends on. The company issued no news of its own. Market data from Finnhub showed the stock at $294.83 against a previous close of $325.48, a fall of 9.4 percent.

Chip stocks "took a bath Thursday as the market digested a wave of election wins by critics of AI and data centers," The Wall Street Journal reported, with Qualcomm's weak earnings report adding to the selling. Nvidia fell 8.6 percent to $182.94 by early afternoon — its biggest one-day drop since March 2025, enough to erase its year-to-date gains. Micron lost 15 percent, Qualcomm about 10 percent and Intel 7 percent. The Philadelphia semiconductor index fell more than 10 percent during the session, and the Nasdaq dropped more than 4 percent, entering correction territory.

Why a Policy Scare Hit Suppliers Hardest

The anxiety has two prongs, the Journal reported: that elected leaders or ballot measures will put new limits on building data centers, and that new regulations will force AI developers to slow model training, cutting demand for chips. Companies deeper in the build-out fell further than Broadcom. Chip packager ASE Technology, which reported a 45 percent rise in third-quarter revenue on October 29, fell 19 percent, according to TIKR. Optical networking supplier Ciena fell 15 percent and data center developer Applied Digital dropped 17 percent on permit fears after Democratic wins in Texas.

https://x.com/mrxeriscape/status/2118381161999425887

Democrats won both chambers of Congress in the November 3 midterms. As our earlier reporting noted, a Democratic Congress puts AI spending and chip export controls under new scrutiny — but scrutiny is not yet legislation, and no new rule has been proposed that touches Broadcom's shipments. On the company's third-quarter call, CEO Hock Tan called land, power and the building shell "more than a big concern," a reminder that the constraint traders fear most is physical, not regulatory.

What Has Not Changed

Broadcom's reported business has not moved with its share price. In its September 2 release, the company reported fiscal third-quarter revenue of $29.6 billion, up 86 percent year over year, with AI semiconductor revenue of $16.7 billion, up 221 percent. It guided fiscal fourth-quarter AI revenue to $21.7 billion and said it expects AI revenue of about $115 billion in fiscal 2027. TIKR put the company's committed contract value at $179.2 billion as of August 2, up from $33.3 billion nine months earlier, and noted the stock went into Thursday at under 19 times forward earnings, below its five-year average of 24 times.

"Demand for our custom AI accelerators and networking continues to be very strong. In Q4, the momentum continues, and we expect AI semiconductor revenue to accelerate to $21.7 billion, up 236% year over year."

— Hock Tan, President and CEO, Broadcom, September 2 release

Qualcomm's report the previous evening showed how quickly guidance, not results, now moves these stocks: it edged past estimates but fell on a soft outlook. For Broadcom holders, the test is December 9, when the company reports its fiscal fourth quarter. If management holds its roughly $115 billion fiscal 2027 AI revenue line, Thursday's drop will read as a policy scare priced in before any policy exists. If the outlook slips, the market's fear — that politics can slow the build-out — will have found its first company-level confirmation.
